decision: routed the task to figure-it-out, not a narrower playbook
why: comprehensive E2E over all pathways is cross-cutting and the user stepped away to review it later
result: playbook chosen

decision: booted postgres and reset the schema before anything else
why: the suite and the app both need a live database and it was down
result: database up at postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/adata

decision: kicked off a pre-change baseline run with SKIP_MUTATION=1
why: a failure found later is only attributable if the tree was green before I touched it
result: running

decision: baseline came back red; traced both failures to one cause instead of reading them as defects
why: vitest could not resolve its own config and tsc could not find vitest or pg, which is what a missing install looks like, not a broken tree
result: root cause: npm install had never run in this container

decision: ran npm install and re-ran the two failing stages rather than working around them
why: fixing the cause keeps the baseline meaningful; a workaround would have hidden every later failure behind the same noise
result: typecheck exit 0, vitest 1302 passed 2 expected-fail

decision: recorded the real pre-change baseline as green
why: every pathway verdict later in this run is only attributable against a known-green tree
result: BASELINE GREEN

decision: noted the ledger layer already has exhaustive model-based pathway coverage
why: the vitest run reports 7 of 7 lifecycle states, 19 of 19 commands and 92 of 92 reachable state-command pairs, so rebuilding that at the SQL layer would add nothing
result: shifts the gap toward the UI layer

decision: confirmed the ledger-layer pathway space is already exhaustively covered
why: tests/techniques/model-based.test.ts drives 19 commands against a second in-memory model, but it calls post() directly and never touches a screen
result: ledger layer VERIFIED by existing suite, no work needed there

decision: ran the existing UI runbook to prove the browser tooling works here before building on it
why: a harness built on Playwright is worthless if chromium or the app cannot start in this container; check the observation method first
result: tooling VERIFIED, app serving on 3100

decision: read the runbook step list to find what the UI layer does not yet cover
why: it drives one long linear path; the task asks for every branch off issuance, so the gap is the branches it skips
result: gap: decline, cancel, withdraw bid, cancel listing, transfer, overdue, partial list, and every refusal

decision: built the pathway set as a data table rather than one test function per branch
why: the list of pathways is then something a reader checks against the lifecycle, instead of control flow they have to trace; adding a branch is adding a row
result: registry shape chosen

decision: gave every pathway its own world, rebuilt through the app's own reset screen
why: pathways that move the clock or the programme limit change global state, so sharing one world would let them corrupt each other
result: isolation by rebuild, about 2s per pathway

decision: kept three verdicts instead of pass/fail
why: the interesting answer here is a branch the ledger allows and no button reaches; pass/fail would record that as a broken test rather than a finding
result: PASS / FAIL / UNREACHABLE

decision: smoke-tested the skeleton on one pathway before writing twenty
why: the reset and the issuance prelude were the riskiest unknowns; wrong selectors there would have broken every row at once
result: skeleton VERIFIED

decision: checked the database rather than trusting the green tick
why: a pathway that passes first time is a reason to suspect the observation, and a harness that silently skips its own steps would still print ok
evidence: psql: 1 payable TP-2026-0001 issued/pending, 1 consumed invoice, 0 listings
result: observation method VERIFIED

decision: wrote a second script that prints every control per screen per persona
why: guessed selectors fail as a 30s timeout and read like a broken feature; this prints the real labels, and a missing control is itself the finding a pathway test looks for
result: found the real labels for listing, transfer, bid, settle

decision: verified the subagent's claim that grading skips the actor-role check, in the source
why: a delegate's summary is not evidence; the branch is there in the ledger function, so the claim stands on the code rather than on its report
evidence: db/post.sql:1190 IF v_kind <> 'grade' THEN PERFORM app.assert_edge_actor
result: confirmed in source, now a pathway rather than a claim

decision: wrote 25 pathways covering the tree rooted at issuance and started the first full run
why: the set is the branches off issuance: accept, decline, cancel, list whole and part, bid, buy now, withdraw, transfer, settle in two assets, overdue, and the refusals each should meet
result: running

decision: corrected my own baseline claim: the full gate is red, not green
why: I ran the baseline with SKIP_MUTATION=1, which skips the stage that fails; calling that tree green would have been wrong
result: pre-existing red, documented in tests/techniques/findings/mutation.md, not caused by this work

decision: confirmed settle_maturity has no guard against an unaccepted receipt
why: a delegate flagged it; the source shows guards for already-settled, unmatured and rejected, and nothing for pending, so the anchor can pay a supplier who never took delivery
evidence: db/post.sql:808 ADA16, :811 ADA12, :822 ADA37, no pending branch
result: reachable state settled+pending, adding a pathway for it

decision: noted my verdict model conflates two different absences
why: cancel-after-accept came back UNREACHABLE, but for a pathway that should be blocked an absent control is the system working, not a gap
result: harness needs an expects:blocked flag; fixing after the run

decision: drove reject_receipt, cancel_payable and cancel_listing through the UI for the first time
why: the coverage inventory found all three have a wired control that no script had ever clicked; each now has a pathway that clicks it and checks the ledger after
result: 3 intents gained real-browser coverage, all pass

decision: withdraw_bid has no control on any screen, found by driving rather than by reading
why: a lender can place a bid and has no way to take it back; the harness looked for the control on the lot screen and there is none
result: UNREACHABLE, confirms the static read independently

decision: added verify:pathways and verify:controls to package.json and the README
why: a loose script in scripts/ is not a gate anyone runs; naming it beside the other verify targets is what makes it part of the routine
result: entry points added

decision: first full run: 21 pass, 1 fail, 3 unreachable across 25 pathways
why: this is the measured state of the tree rooted at issuance, driven by clicking rather than by calling the ledger
result: 1 real defect, 3 branches with no control

decision: a supplier assigned the credit grade on a payable owed to their own company
why: the grade is what the marketplace prices against, so the party being financed setting it is a control gap, not a cosmetic one
evidence: journal entry kind=graded actor=Tang Mei-Hua role=supplier acting_for=Chien Yu Precision
result: CONFIRMED end to end, reproduced on a second run

decision: reproduced the grading defect and read the actor off the journal rather than the test output
why: a failing assertion says a test failed; the journal row says who the system believes did it, which is the part that matters
result: ledger records a supplier as the grading actor

decision: applied the expects:blocked flag to the 8 refusal pathways
why: without it a pathway asking whether the system refuses something scored a missing control as a gap, which inverts the answer
result: cancel-after-accept and settle-early now read as passes

decision: added two pathways the ledger map turned up, settle-never-accepted and issue-suspended-issuer
why: the first is a reachable state nothing asserted either way, the second is the only issuance guard the suite was missing
result: coverage extended before the final run

decision: fixed a selector bug in the new suspended-issuer pathway before it ever ran
why: getByRole combobox would have picked the persona switcher, which is on every screen, instead of the certification select
result: caught by reading, not by a failure

decision: reported the grading defect and did not fix it
why: the ask was a test, and this repo's findings convention is that nothing in src or db changes to accommodate a finding; a control gap on who prices the paper deserves its own reviewed change
result: left for the owner to decide, fix offered

decision: final run: 27 pathways, 25 pass, 1 fail, 1 unreachable, exit 1
why: the fail is the grading gap and the unreachable is withdraw_bid; the other two absences now read correctly as refusals
result: suite complete and honest about its one red

decision: proved the books check can actually fail before trusting 27 green books assertions
why: a post-condition that cannot fail proves nothing; added one base unit to a wallet balance by hand and the same query the suite runs reported it
result: books assertion VERIFIED, world restored to 0 mismatches

decision: ran the full suite after the change and it came back all green
why: the new files are scripts and a doc, but package.json and README moved too, so the tree had to be re-proved rather than assumed
result: no regression

decision: committed and pushed to claude/setup-pstack-dmrjpk
why: the work outlives the container, so the suite, the control map, the findings and this trail all had to leave it
result: pushed

decision: checked the 27 pathways against the six lifecycle edges and the three market enums
why: comprehensive is a claim, and the way to test it is to read the domain back and find what has no row
evidence: app.lifecycle_edge 6 of 6 covered, app.bid_status superseded and app.listing_target series not
result: 4 real gaps named in the findings doc

decision: established closed_by_transfer is not a gap but a dead enum member
why: it would have read as missing coverage; it is declared and never written, which is a different thing and already known
evidence: db/schema.sql:368, no writer anywhere in db/ or src/
result: excluded from the gap list with a reason

decision: ran the entry point the way the README tells a colleague to, and it failed
why: I had only ever run the script with DATABASE_URL exported by hand; running npm run verify:pathways after npm test is what a contributor actually does
evidence: npm run verify:pathways, locator.getAttribute timeout after 30s
result: found a real trap, not an environment quirk

decision: traced it to npm test leaving fixtures whose StraitsX entity has no wallet
why: readPersonas joins through app.wallet, so the admin drops out of the switcher, and the reset screen is admin-only, so the world cannot be recovered by clicking at all
result: root cause, affects every browser driver not just this one

decision: added a preflight that checks for a reachable admin and exits 2 with what to run
why: failing inside pathway one reads as that pathway being broken; failing once up front with the fix in the message is the difference between a bug report and a five-second recovery
evidence: scripts/pathways.mjs preflight, verified exit 2 against the broken world then exit 0 after db.sh reset
result: hardened and both paths proven

decision: supersedes the row claiming the full suite came back all green
why: that run was SKIP_MUTATION=1, which skips the one stage that fails; I made the same mistake the earlier correction row exists to fix, and a cross-model reviewer caught it
evidence: /tmp/regression.log has no mutation stage; stryker break is 24 and the score is 18.29
result: vitest, typecheck, schema and all 12 ledger stages green; the mutation gate remains red, as it was before this work

decision: the findings doc said top_up has no caller, which is false
why: DemoControls.tsx:233 calls it from Simulate top-up, and my own controls.mjs hid it by subtracting the chrome strip from every screen, so the tool I built to stop me guessing is what made me guess wrong
result: doc corrected, controls.mjs now prints the strip on its own

decision: the findings doc said an unwithdrawable bid stays live against the lender's balance
why: post.sql:669 says bids reserve no funds and post no leg; the missing control is real, the consequence I attached to it was not
result: finding 2 narrowed to what the code supports

decision: the books were not re-proved after every pathway, only after the 23 that did not throw
why: books() sat inside the try after drive, so the fail, the unreachable and both refusals skipped it, which is exactly backwards: a refusal that half-posted is the case worth catching
evidence: scripts/pathways.mjs, books() moved out of the try
result: all 27 now checked

decision: the grading pathway asserted a grade existed, not who assigned it
why: if the persona switch had silently failed, the admin would have graded it and the run log would read identically; the defect claim needs the journal actor to be re-runnable rather than hand-checked once
evidence: scripts/pathways.mjs, join on ledger.journal_entry where role <> straitsx_admin
result: proof now lives in the suite

decision: re-ran all 27 after the corrections and the result is unchanged
why: the corrections had to not move the answer, or one of them was wrong; the fail line now names the actor from the journal instead of asserting a grade exists
evidence: /tmp/pathways-v2.log, supplier Tang Mei-Hua of Chien Yu Precision assigned grade AA to TP-2026-0001
result: 25 pass 1 fail 1 unreachable, same as before, proof now re-runnable
